title: 5 ways Amazon is investing in Connecticut
summary: Amazon's investments are boosting the Constitution State's economy while creating opportunities for those who call Connecticut home.
body_markdown:
---


## Key takeaways


- Amazon has


[invested more than $12 billion](https://assets.aboutamazon.com/d4/08/a307af1e4378a90621789e1110d4/amazoninvestment-connecticut-2025.pdf) in Connecticut and contributed over $10 billion to the state's economy.


- The company has more than 15,000 full- and part-time employees and supports more than 10,000 indirect jobs.


- Amazon partners with three educational institutions in Connecticut through its


[Career Choice](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/workplace/career-choice-free-education-for-amazon-employees) program and has upskilled over 2,100 employees since 2019.


- Connecticut-based independent sellers sold over 42 million items through Amazon's store.


---


For more than 30 years, Amazon has been investing across the United States, strengthening local economies and creating opportunities for communities nationwide. Connecticut is a prime example of this commitment, with Amazon building a substantial presence in the state since 2015.


Amazon associate Tomin Kurian Kalarickal at Amazon BDL4 Windsor, CT, a 3.8-million-square-foot robotics-powered fulfillment center in Windsor, Connecticut.


Today, Connecticut serves as a thriving logistics hub for Amazon, with investments spanning fulfillment centers to Whole Foods Market locations. The company's economic impact extends beyond direct employment, supporting thousands of additional jobs in construction, logistics, and professional services, and helping local businesses reach customers around the world.


Here are five ways Amazon is investing in Connecticut.


## 1. Investing in our employees


Amazon provides


[competitive wages and comprehensive benefits from Day 1](https://www.aboutamazon.com/workplace/employee-benefits) . Core operations full-time employees earn an average hourly base wage of nearly $24, with total compensation averaging more than $32 an hour when including benefits. These benefits include health, vision, and dental insurance starting on Day 1, free mental health resources, up to 20 weeks of fully paid parental leave, a 401(k) with 50% company match, and flexible time-off options that increase with tenure.


Amazon Area Manager Hope Turner and Associate Ashley Garcia at Amazon BDL4.


Beyond more than 15,000 direct jobs, Amazon's presence in Connecticut supports more than 10,000 indirect jobs in industries such as construction, logistics, and professional services—suppliers and partners whom we rely on every day.


## 2. Supporting workforce development and upskilling


Amazon is committed to preparing its workforce for future opportunities through comprehensive education and skills training programs. Since 2019, more than 2,100 Connecticut employees have participated in these free initiatives.


[Amazon commits $1 billion to Career Choice employee education program as part of Future Ready 2030 fund](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/workplace/amazon-future-of-work-skills-jobs-training)


The Future Ready 2030 fund supports students, employees, and those looking to expand their skills as the workforce adapts to a changing economy.


In Connecticut, Amazon partners with three educational institutions through its


[Career Choice program](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/workplace/career-choice-free-education-for-amazon-employees) , which prepays tuition for employees pursuing further education. These partnerships with colleges and universities across the state help Amazon employees gain in-demand skills that can propel them into new careers.


Amazon employees Neil Brown and Jose Colon at Amazon BDL4 Windsor, CT, a 3.8-million-square-foot robotics-powered fulfillment center in Windsor, Connecticut, U.S. August 5, 2026.


From Machine Learning University to Career Choice, these programs represent Amazon's investment in developing talent and creating pathways to opportunity for its workforce.


## 3. Building infrastructure across the Constitution State


Since 2010, Amazon has invested more than $12 billion in Connecticut's infrastructure and employee compensation, contributing more than $10 billion to the state's gross domestic product.


Amazon associate Yamilet Maysonet at Amazon BDL4.


These investments include six


[fulfillment and sortation centers](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/tag/fulfillment-center) , 11 delivery stations, and other facilities across the state. The company has also expanded its retail footprint with 13


[Whole Foods Market locations](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/tag/whole-foods-market) across Connecticut. Amazon continues to grow its sustainable infrastructure as well, with six solar farms and six sites with on-site solar power in the state.


## 4. Empowering Connecticut's small businesses


Amazon provides a powerful opportunity for Connecticut's entrepreneurs and small businesses to reach customers worldwide. Connecticut-based independent sellers—primarily small and medium-sized businesses—sold more than 42 million items through Amazon's store, with the average seller generating more than $275,000 in annual sales.


Inside


[Mystic Knotwork](https://sellingpartners.aboutamazon.com/mystic-company-finds-modern-audience-for-traditional-handcrafted-nautical-products)


's shop in historic downtown Mystic, where the art of handcrafted nautical knots has been a family tradition since the 1960s.


These independent sellers represent more than 60% of sales in Amazon's store. Their success contributes significantly to local economies, with more than 65% of U.S. independent sellers employing at least one person within 50 miles of their primary business location.


By providing infrastructure, logistics support, and access to millions of customers, Amazon enables Connecticut's small businesses to scale their operations and create additional jobs throughout the state.


## 5. Investing as a good neighbor


Amazon uses its global scale and strengths to make a positive impact in communities. Working with trusted community partners, we address critical needs—


[food security](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/tag/hunger) ,


[education](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/tag/education) ,


[disaster relief](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/community/amazon-delivers-disaster-relief-in-response-to-kentucky-flooding) —using our logistics, technology, and innovation, while investing as a good neighbor in the communities where our employees live and work.


Team members from Amazon's Black Employee Network sorted 4,913 pounds of dry goods while volunteering at a Connecticut food bank.


Amazon has delivered more than 900,000 meals on behalf of food banks and nonprofits across the state. The company has reached more than 20,000 students and 800 teachers through education programs and supported more than 200,000 computer science learning hours. More than 700 Amazon employees have volunteered in communities across Connecticut.
